quotes.text: Learn how to accept MobilePay, a popular payment method in Denmark and Finland.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: When the PaymentIntent’s status is `requires_action`, your customer must authenticate the payment within 5 minutes.
Stripe only support manual captures of the full amount.

This guide covers how to accept MobilePay from your native mobile application using your own custom payment form. Your native mobile application redirects your customer to a webview to complete the payment on MobilePay.

findings: The 2026-11-07 capture is a navigation index, retaining the May introduction naming Denmark and Finland and linking the same Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android, and React Native variants. It provides zero variant bodies, prerequisites, or transaction states (new raw lines 1–19; old raw lines 1–10, 229–231, 833–835, 1084–1086, 1381–1383, 1605–1607; diff lines 1–13 and 1887–1895).

The baseline omits React Native in the list on source lines 13–17 and miscounts four web paths. Old raw lines 8–10, 229–231, 833–835, 1084–1086, 1381–1383, and 1605–1607 identify Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android, and React Native. Checkout itself illustrates hosted and embedded presentations at old raw lines 59–117. New raw lines 9–19 lists the same six variants. A React Native integrator can reasonably rule out MobilePay from reading the explicit source list, and the unspecific link at source line 35 does not surface the relevant historical SDK section.

Source lines 13 and 21 call the five minutes an authorization window. Old raw lines 213–217, 995–1006 and 1880–1884 scope it to customer authentication while the PaymentIntent is in requires_action. The PaymentMethod detaches on timeout and the PaymentIntent returns to requires_payment_method. This wording matters for readers looking for a deadline to capture an already-authorized payment, a separate state shown at old raw lines 190–205, 800–815 and 1051–1066. Full-amount manual capture is documented in Checkout, Elements and Direct API there, and those sections do not establish it for every mobile variant.

Source line 19 is accurate for the dated manual Checkout configuration but leaves out the dynamic path described in old raw lines 16–22. Source lines 23–29 can retain their historical details when the Direct API redirect destination field, Android MobilePay-specific payment method params and pre-expiry cancellation are kept in their distinct contexts (old raw lines 958–1006, 1070–1078 and 1535–1544).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Actual capture is 2026-05-07 per old raw line 2, regardless of the -2025 filename. Historical old raw lines 12–40 and 55–117 describe a single-use card wallet and Stripe processing the underlying card transaction, EEA Checkout business location, listed EUR/DKK/SEK/NOK line-item currencies, payment mode only, and dynamic versus manual selection. The Checkout Session examples are UI-scoped.

Old raw lines 252–296, 365–379, 412–414, 515–517 and 611–748 cover the Elements path with server-created PaymentIntent and client-side confirmation, client-secret handling, return URL and PaymentIntent status for customer messaging, and Stripe events for post-payment actions. An automatic-payment-method code sample uses USD at lines 258–273, without establishing MobilePay USD eligibility.

Old raw lines 854–885 and 958–1025 show server-side Direct API create and confirm by PaymentIntent ID and the customer-action URL at next_action.redirect_to_url.url. The initial requires_confirmation and subsequent requires_action in that example are different from payment success; test authorization/failure is explicitly a test flow. Old raw lines 125–153 and 744–774 distinguish test redirects from live device behavior.

Old raw lines 155–221, 776–831 and 1027–1082 describe full-amount manual capture after requires_capture and payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated, distinct from the requires_action timeout; cancellation is for the associated PaymentIntent before expiry and refunds/disputes follow card-network rules.

May platform scopes remain dated. iOS' custom-scheme return and SDK callback, Android's PaymentLauncher and MobilePay-specific params, and React Native's webview, case-sensitive MobilePay method value and iOS-only custom return configuration remain distinct (old raw lines 1239–1346, 1510–1570 and 1748–1855). iOS 13+ wording and the Android 23.7.0 example at old raw lines 1111–1114 and 1408–1433 are historical SDK context rather than November requirements.
conflicts: Variant count and React Native omission are pre-existing wiki discrepancies, not a November launch. The wrong list/count and ambiguous five-minute label also surface via wiki/concepts/stripe-wallets.md lines 235 and 415, wiki/stripe-index.md line 407 and wiki/companies/stripe.md line 604. Correct or qualify the reciprocal routes so they do not restate the baseline issue.

No contrary November behavioral statement. The separate MobilePay overview reports partial refunds (wiki/sources/source-stripe-mobilepay.md line 21), while the May acceptance guide restricts the documented manual capture to the full amount (old raw lines 190–205, 800–815 and 1051–1066). Refund and capture are distinct operations.
unresolved_questions: The November variant bodies were outside this capture. The two pinned captures cannot establish current variant behavior, account eligibility, SDK requirements, or any live outcome.

source_assessments.reason: Source correction is needed for the pre-existing path count, omitted React Native integration, and misleading use of authorization window without the customer-action condition. Retain and date the detailed May authority and route the November capture as an index.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-19 describes MobilePay as popular in Denmark and Finland and links Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native. The fetched base URL leaves payment prerequisites, integration mechanics and transaction states to individual variants. The May 7 capture identifies MobilePay as a single-use wallet that uses an underlying card transaction. It documents dynamic or manual Checkout Session configuration, EEA businesses, EUR/DKK/SEK/NOK line items and payment mode without setup or subscriptions (old raw lines 12-40 and 55-117). It distinguishes server-created PaymentIntents from client-side Elements and SDK confirmation, and directs Direct API clients to the customer-action URL after server confirmation (old raw lines 252-296, 515-517 and 854-1006). Customer authentication while in requires_action has five minutes before the PaymentMethod detaches and the Intent returns to requires_payment_method. For the documented manual-capture paths, successful authorization instead reaches requires_capture and full-amount capture can follow. Post-payment actions use payment_intent.succeeded (old raw lines 123-127, 155-217 and 1027-1078). source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md lines 13-23 compresses these facts into an ambiguous authorization window, miscounts the web variants, and omits the historically documented React Native SDK flow (old raw lines 1605-1888).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 9-19 reflects a navigation change. The linked November bodies are unread and the index supplies no substantive payment change or deprecation evidence. Keep the six detailed variants dated to 2026-05-07, including the Checkout mode and currency constraints, Elements server/client split and status check, Direct API's next_action.redirect_to_url.url, and the native SDK-specific confirmation and return handling (old raw lines 24-40, 252-296, 515-517, 611-748, 958-1006, 1239-1346, 1510-1570 and 1748-1855). In source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md and its reciprocal Wallets, Stripe index, and company routes, repair the baseline miscount and React Native omission and specify that the five minutes is a customer authentication deadline in requires_action. Full manual capture after requires_capture is documented for Checkout, Elements and Direct API, and concerns the capture amount rather than refund options (old raw lines 155-221, 776-831 and 1027-1082). Keep historical SDK versions, examples and test/live paths qualified. Redirect or callback delivery, resource creation, and customer authentication each precede or differ from verified payment completion. The historical guide uses PaymentIntent status for customer messaging and payment_intent.succeeded for consequential post-payment actions (old raw lines 123-153, 611-665 and 744-774).
